hints.title: Find Exact Median
hints.text: Sort the array. The median is arr[(n - 1) // 2].

hints.title: Strongest Value Definition
hints.text: Element x is stronger than y if abs(x - m) > abs(y - m), or if abs(x - m) == abs(y - m) and x > y.

hints.title: Two Pointer Boundary Pick
hints.text: In the sorted array, candidates for strongest elements are always at the outer extremes (left or right). Pick k elements.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def getStrongest(self, arr: list[int], k: int) -> list[int]:
        arr.sort()
        n = len(arr)
        m = arr[(n - 1) // 2]
        left, right = 0, n - 1
        res = []
        for _ in range(k):
            if abs(arr[right] - m) >= abs(arr[left] - m):
                res.append(arr[right])
                right -= 1
            else:
                res.append(arr[left])
                left += 1
        return res
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Full custom sort of all elements by strength works in O(N log N); using two pointers after sorting takes O(K) selection.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting once then converging two pointers from ends picks the k strongest values in O(N log N + K).
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate sorts to find median and uses two pointers at ends to greedily take strongest elements.
